name: Shut Behind You
hint: Two takes, and the door you need SHUT is the one that starts open. d1 at x=13.5 is a portcullis: open until switch s1 fires, then it seals (its bulkhead runs from y=14 up to y=0, so there is no route over it, and the west stack only climbs to y=14.4 on the wrong side of it). d2 at x=30 is the opposite — sealed until s1 fires. s1 lapses after 6 seconds, so the level contains exactly one 6-second window in which d1 is shut and d2 is open. TAKE 1: from spawn (x=10, floor top y=20) walk LEFT 3.5 units to x=6.5 and jump up-left 2.8 onto the ledge at y=17.2 (x=4.0..7.0); walk to its left edge at x=4.0 and jump up-left another 2.8 onto the ledge at y=14.4 (x=0..3.2); walk left and interact with s1 at x=1.0..2.0, at about t=1.6s. Throw it ONCE and then stand still — a second interact is recorded too and would re-toggle the switch in the replay. The moment you throw it, d1 seals 12 units below and to your right: d2 is now open but d1 is between you and it, so nobody who throws this switch ever uses it. Wait out the 6 seconds and you only trade one shut door for the other, forever. End the take up on the ledge. TAKE 2: your Echo repeats the climb and throws s1 at about t=1.6s. RUN RIGHT the instant the take starts — your body has to be past x=14.7 before the throw, which is 4.8 units, 0.52s at 9.2 u/s, so you clear the portcullis with ~0.9s to spare even against a perfectly efficient take 1. Do not stop: the floor ends at x=20, jump the 4.0-unit pit (inside the 6.0 budget) and land at about x=24.4 at t≈1.55s, reach d2 at x=30 at t≈2.16s — it swept open at about t≈1.95s — pass through and walk into the exit at x=35.5 by t≈2.8s, roughly three seconds into a six-second window. If your take 1 was slower, just run to the doorway and wait there; the window opens when the Echo throws, not when you arrive.

dialogue.text: That doorway is already open. The switch on the west stack is what shuts it.

dialogue.speaker: ECHO-0
dialogue.text: So the throw has to land after you are through. Which means it cannot be you who throws it.
Six seconds of open door on the far side. Don't stop to watch the near one close.
